name.text: Surface area of a cylindrical flower vase

questiontext.text:
{@student_name@} had an art project of painting the external surface of a cylindrical flower pot. The flower pot has a radius of {@radius@} cm and a height of {@height@} cm. Calculate the total external surface area that {@student_name@} painted.

Give your answer in cm2, correct to the nearest whole number.

Surface area = [[input:ans1]] \( \text{cm}^2 \)[[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Solution

The flower pot is a cylinder that is open at the top.

To find the external surface area, include:

  • the curved surface area of the cylinder, and
  • the circular base.

Using \(\pi \approx {@pi_value@}\)

The curved surface area of a cylinder is:

\[ 2\pi rh \]

Substituting \(r={@radius@}\) cm, \(h={@height@}\) cm and \(\pi={@pi_value@}\):

\[ 2\times {@pi_value@}\times {@radius@}\times {@height@} = {@curved_area@}\text{ cm}^2 \]

The area of the circular base is:

\[ \pi r^2 \]

Substituting \(r={@radius@}\) cm and \(\pi={@pi_value@}\):

\[ {@pi_value@}\times {@radius@}^2 = {@base_area@}\text{ cm}^2 \]

Adding these areas:

\[ {@curved_area@} + {@base_area@} = {@Total_surface_area@}\text{ cm}^2 \]

Therefore, the total external surface area painted is {@Total_surface_area@} cm2.
